info.name: Receipt notes - Batches and inventory transfers
info.description:
# Receipt batches and inventory transfers

Importable Postman Collection v2.1. All saved responses are illustrative, abridged where stated, and contain synthetic data; they are not captured production responses. No scripts execute requests or retry failed writes.

## Environments and authentication
- UAT: https://zuat-accounting-back.myt-emr.com
- Production: https://accounting-back.myt-emr.com
- Set base_url, the normal API-KEY header, requester and token. Credentials are blank. Existing master authentication, permissions and branch restrictions apply. This collection does not add CSR access.
- Branches: 1 Mobile, 2 Oakridge, 3 Mactan, 4 Consolacion, 5 Warehouse, 6 Pharmacy, 7 Mantlewood.
- Use form-data for POST; Postman supplies the multipart boundary. Nested item fields use PHP bracket notation. Replace all record-ID variables with authorized, existing records before intentional use.

## Receipt batches (deployed to UAT and production on October 16, 2026)
All three batch columns use nullable VARCHAR(255) with utf8mb4_bin collation; compatible wider columns remain wider. receipt_note_item.batch_no contains CSV codes; expiry_dates[].batch_no and transfer-line batch_no contain single string codes. The schema conversion is installed across master and all seven inventory schemas in both environments. Existing integer values were preserved as strings, together with defaults, comments and indexes. No stock/accounting backfill was performed; existing deployed PHP files were preserved.
Codes accept printable UTF-8 text, including letters, digits, punctuation and internal spaces, up to 255 characters. Trim surrounding spaces; commas delimit the parent CSV and are forbidden within an individual code. Control characters and invalid UTF-8 are rejected. Null/blank values are absent. Non-negative integer inputs remain accepted for compatibility and become strings; API examples use quoted strings. Numeric-looking strings are not normalized: AB123, ab123, 0012 and 12 are four distinct codes. Zero is returned as "0".
Parent CSV codes are deduplicated in submitted order and must match the distinct non-null child codes as exact case-sensitive string sets, regardless of order. The normalized parent CSV must fit 255 characters. Repeated codes across expiry dates remain supported; expiry quantities are non-negative and cannot exceed the parent item qty in total. Partial allocation remains allowed.
Create and update validate the entire submitted item list before writes. On retained rows, an omitted batch key retains its saved value; explicit null clears it if resulting parent/child sets remain consistent. Multipart blank fields normalize to null. Update keeps the existing full-selection replacement behavior: submit every retained item and expiry ID, or omitted rows are soft-deleted. Ordinary update with omitted items can remove existing items; do not treat it as a patch. Existing APV-screen behavior is unchanged. GET returns items[].batch_no and items[].expiry_dates[].batch_no.
Receipt writes still require an approved purchase order, supplier, needed_date, valid branch/item/unit links, and existing cost/pricing validations. UAT retains its disabled receipt-create attachment step; production retains normal attachment processing. Optional uploads use attachments[] with parallel attachment_types[] values dr or si.

## Transfer availability and receipt
Each transfer line has one optional string batch_no. Split the same item into separate lines for different batches. Submit item_id, branch_item_id, unit and positive transfer_qty (up to four decimal places). Source/destination must differ and be branches 1 through 7. A pending transfer for the same branch pair prevents a second submission.
Labelled availability uses source-branch approved active expiry qty_balance, less outstanding reservations from active pending/approved/opened transfers. Null balances are zero; original qty and historical transfer arithmetic are not fallbacks. Explicitly linked lines also require sufficient balance in their selected allocation. Unlabelled lines use branch-local branch_item.current_qty, less outstanding reservations; master inventory quantities are not a substitute. Existing item conversions put comparisons into a common unit; total source stock is also checked, including unlabelled transfers. Receipt expiry rows allocate batches; the parent receipt quantity is not counted again. Sales, consumption and adjustments are not batch-attributed, so batch availability is not a complete lot ledger.
Submission reserves quantity without moving stock. Approval rechecks availability. Receive with status=received and parallel transfer_item_ids[] / received_qtys[] arrays. Received quantities are cumulative: 3 followed by 5 moves 3 then 2. Repeating an unchanged receipt, decreasing quantities, over-receiving, or receiving a terminal transfer is rejected. Partial receipt returns the ordinary success message and leaves the saved status opened; inspect get_transfer for that status. Receiving is supported from pending, approved or opened. Legacy item_ids[] is accepted only when each item resolves to exactly one line; never send both ID formats. Only pending transfers may be approved. Disapproval before any stock movement releases reservations; it is rejected after movement.

## Item filters and batch lookup (local implementation only)
GET /items/get_item_filters returns {data:{brand:[],generic:[],dosage:[],form:[]}}. These are independent alphabetically ordered distinct values from non-deleted master items. Null and blank values are excluded; an empty catalog returns four empty arrays with HTTP 200. No branch parameter is needed.
GET /items/get_item_batches requires positive item_id, branch_id_to from 1 through 7, and a real date in YYYY-MM-DD format. branch_id_to chooses the database connection and the matching receipt branch. Only active expiry rows, receipt items, items and approved receipt headers qualify. The cutoff is expiry.date >= date (inclusive), not receipt creation/receive date. Return distinct non-null string batch_no values in lexicographic order, including "0", as {size,data:[{batch_no:0},{batch_no:12}]}. Empty matches return HTTP 404. This is a receipt batch list, not an available-stock or unexpired-batch guarantee. Transfer submission still applies its existing source-stock and reservation validation. There is no automatic submission or modification of transfers.

## Transfer report (receipt starting rows are local only)
Optional term searches only item.name using a bound substring LIKE match across receipt and transfer rows. Null, omitted, empty and whitespace-only terms apply no name filter; surrounding whitespace is trimmed and "0" is a valid search string. Other types return HTTP 400: term must be a string or null. Existing database collation and SQL LIKE wildcard behavior (% and _) are retained. The name filter combines with every other filter using AND and applies equally to rows/counts before pagination. Item-name search remains local only; it is not deployed to UAT or production.
GET /items/transfer_report accepts optional positive item_id and optional exact string batch_no (including "0"). Omitted/blank/null item_id or batch_no applies no corresponding filter. Optional brand, generic, dosage and form are exact whole-field matches; null/blank text filters apply no restriction. kind accepts comma-separated complete tokens, trimmed and deduplicated, with OR matching inside the kind filter. Different filters are combined with AND. Non-string text filters return HTTP 400. page/data_size retain existing positive-integer pagination.
Returns {size,data} with the full matching count across individual receipt allocations and grouped received transfers. Approved active receipt headers, items and expiry allocations with nonblank batch codes produce one activity="Receipt" row per expiry allocation, even without any transfer. Repeated allocations of the same batch remain separate. quantity contains the stored expiry-row qty_balance, including zero or null, without falling back to original qty. beginning_qty contains the original expiry-row qty. Receipt rows remain visible after partial or full transfers; quantity reflects the current stored balance while beginning_qty stays unchanged. Receipt rows carry branch_id/name, receipt_note_id, receipt_note_item_id, expiry_id, expiry_date, item metadata and the receipt unit/conversion. Transfer-specific fields and current_qty are null. movement_date uses receipt.receive_date or, when absent, receipt.added_on; expiry_date is not the movement date. Read each receipt only from its configured source branch, including Warehouse and Pharmacy; do not count mirrored copies.
Active transfer lines with received_qty > 0 and non-null batch_no qualify for grouping alongside individual receipts. Transfer groups sum cumulative received quantities in quantity and requested quantities in transfer_qty. Valid linked source receipt IDs are returned as distinct CSV strings; expiry_id and expiry_date remain null. Pending/unreceived lines, unlabelled transfers, unlabelled beginning inventory and No movement placeholder rows remain excluded. Items without qualifying receipts or transfers return the standard HTTP 404 response. Transfer movements are read from master without mirrored duplicates.
Rows include item.brand, generic, dosage, form and kind. Units/conversions and branch names remain available; quantities in different units are never added together. The report does not create a separate row for each partial-receipt event. Order primarily by batch_no in case-sensitive ascending text order before pagination (for example: 0, 0012, 10, 2, AB123, ab123). Within each batch, retain earliest contributing movement date, Receipt first on equal dates, and deterministic item, branch, source and unit keys. Counts use the same combined filters and grouped result.
This receipt-row extension is local only and has not been deployed. The earlier alphanumeric batch schema and lookup endpoints were deployed on October 16, 2026. Normal API-KEY, requester/token and permission handling apply; this collection adds no CSR access.

## Errors and partial-mirror recovery
Errors use Core's {status,error,messages:{error_messages:[...]}} envelope. 400 covers validation, insufficient stock/batch, invalid transitions and operation failures; 401 covers authentication/permissions; 404 covers missing/list results.
The existing mirror workflow uses separate connections. A late mirror, cost, status or outer commit failure may leave earlier mirror writes committed even if master rolls back. Stop before retrying; inspect the transfer, all inventory mirrors, history and cost trails and reconcile under controlled maintenance. No automatic retry or repair is included.


Receipt allocation linkage (local only): every populated items[n][batch_no], including "0", requires items[n][receipt_note_item_expiry_date_id] as a positive integer from the branch_id_from database. The active allocation must match the item and exact batch code under an approved active receipt. Without a batch, omit this ID or pass null/blank; a populated ID is rejected. Repeated selections share the selected row balance, less outstanding reservations, with existing aggregate batch and source-stock checks retained. New receipt quantities deduct only from the selected allocation; they cannot spill into another row. Existing null-ID batched transfers continue pooled processing while protecting linked reservations. No historical linkage is assigned.

## Grouped Transfer rows
Transfer grouping (local only): combine Transfer rows by branch_id_from, branch_id_to, item_id, exact case-sensitive batch_no, conversion_type and unit ID, across transfer headers and dates. Different units remain separate. Sum beginning_qty, quantity, current_qty and transfer_qty in SQL; all-null sums remain null. transfer_id, transfer_item_id, receipt_note_id, receipt_note_item_id and movement_date are distinct CSV strings, omitting null/blank values; all-missing references return null. IDs sort numerically and dates chronologically. Source receipt references come only from valid active approved linked source-branch allocations; missing/deleted or legacy null links do not remove movements. Shared metadata remains scalar; branch_item_id becomes null if contributing IDs differ or are mixed with null. Transfer expiry_id/expiry_date remain null. Receipt rows remain individual with quantity=qty_balance and beginning_qty=qty. Filters apply before grouping; size counts Transfer groups plus Receipt allocations. Global pagination follows batch_no in case-sensitive ascending text order first, then earliest contributing movement date, Receipt first on equal dates, and deterministic item/branch/source/unit keys. Batch strings and leading zeros are unchanged; this is text order, so 10 precedes 2 and AB123 precedes ab123. Long CSV values are assembled without GROUP_CONCAT truncation.
